statement: For any fixed strictly elliptic nearest-neighbor environment on Z^d and fixed nonzero l, if P_omega^x(X_n·l -> +infinity)>0 at one site x, then it is positive at every site y.
assumptions: all transition probabilities along nearest-neighbor edges are strictly positive
source: own derivation from the Markov property; historical target Drewitz-Ramirez, Open Question 3.2
proof: Fix y and a finite nearest-neighbor path y=x_0,...,x_m=x. Its quenched probability c is a product of positive transition probabilities. Conditional on this path, the future from x has event A_l with probability q_omega(x); adding a finite prefix preserves X_n·l -> +infinity. Hence q_omega(y)>=c q_omega(x)>0.

statement: Under iid strictly elliptic rows, the environment event that directional escape has positive quenched probability from one (equivalently every) site has probability zero or one.
source: own derivation using C0044-w581-01 and ergodicity of iid shifts
proof: Countably many rows and edges give strict ellipticity simultaneously almost surely. By C0044-w581-01, positivity is equivalent at all starts. Shifting the environment changes the start but not whether positive escape is possible, since finite translation of the path leaves its limiting projection unchanged. Thus the event is invariant under all lattice translations. The iid product law is shift ergodic, so its probability is zero or one.
